atoms.sound: ssml: There are 1,000 grams in 1 kilogram. It is easier to give the measurements of heavy things in kilograms rather than grams.
atoms.text: There are 1,000 grams in 1 kilogram. It is easier to give the measurements of heavy things in kilograms rather than grams.

atoms.sound: ssml: For example, if something weighs 1,500 grams, we would usually say it weighs 1.5 kilograms.
atoms.text: For example, if something weighs 1,500 grams, we would usually say it weighs 1.5 kilograms.

atoms.b: We use ((++grams centimetres)) and kilograms to measure the mass of different objects.
There are ((900 ++1,000 2,000)) grams in one kilogram.
If something weighs over 1,000 grams, we usually give its weight in ((++kilograms metres)).
For example, if something weighs 2,000 grams, we say that it weighs ((++2 20 200)) kilograms.
A kilogram of any object will always weigh ((100 ++1,000)) grams.
One kilogram is much ((++heavier lighter)) than one gram.

instruction.text: Which is heavier, 1 kilogram of grapes or 1 kilogram of rocks?

end.text: Even though one rock is heavier than one grape, 1 kilogram of each will weigh the same.
